title: Northline Home — network redesign
decision_question: Should Northline Home close its East regional distribution center in 2027 or retain and optimize it?

initial_hypothesis.statement: Keep the East hub through 2027 because Central capacity and service cannot safely absorb the move.
initial_hypothesis.explanation: The proposed central consolidation yields little net annual saving, violates service in modeled conditions and exhausts capacity; keeping East is reasonable subject to a measurable optimization and future cross-dock gate.

key_insights.text: East fixed cost saved is $1.30M but higher Eastern freight adds $1.00M and handling $0.20M; net annual saving only $0.10M before exit fee.
Central load after full East closure would be 360,000, exactly its practical capacity, and 2028 forecast rises to 389,600.
Modeled Eastern two-day rate falls 96% to 84%, but the contract tests company-wide 92%; aggregate service must be calculated on comparable all-ZIP orders.
98% internal East on-time claim excludes rural ZIPs and must not replace 96% contracted measure.
Cross-dock had 93% performance over a limited six-week pilot, not a contract guarantee for peak season.
Keep and optimize saves $0.30M annually for $0.15M systems spend, with a 2029 lease option preserved.

required_calculations.text: Full close incremental transport and handling
Annual net saving of closing East

decision_relevant_evidence.text: Two-day all-order service floor and Central capacity cap
Fixed plus freight/handling cost and one-time exit charge

contradictory_evidence: 98% selective-ZIP internal KPI vs 96% contract-compliant East rate
Retention premium correlated with Eastern sales coverage
Fixed cost removed vs added transport and damage

reasoning_traps.text: Counting $1.30M gross facility savings as net saving
Treating Eastern SLA as network-wide without weighting
Ignoring Central capacity once Eastern and Central volume grow
Treating six-week cross-dock pilot as peak-season proof

key_tradeoffs.text: Consolidation now vs reversible lease option

plausible_recommendations.text: Keep East in 2027, take verified $0.30M efficiency programme, and test a properly specified peak-season cross-dock contract.
Move selected East lanes to a partner if contractual all-ZIP SLA, capacity and net cost are proven; preserve the 2029 lease option.
Close East and shift all orders to Central without extra capacity or SLA mitigation.

defensibility_criteria: Model all-in cost not warehouse rent only
Weight SLA using all shipments and same ZIP definition
Quantify a realistic alternative and decision gate

decision_requirements.question: Does the recommendation satisfy company-wide service SLA?
Does Central stay within certified capacity under growth?
Is net cost based on comparable definitions?
Is the outsourced option assessed fairly?
decision_requirements.unnecessary_if: if it cannot satisfy an explicit service floor
